diacritics.name: Centralized
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Centralized'
diacritics.reason: This table reads 'centralized' as a move to the central column of the chart, which is [-front, -back]. PanPhon's rule for it changes no feature.

diacritics.name: Advanced tongue root
diacritics.source: Casali (2007), 'Some observations on the phonetics of [ATR] contrasts', lecture, University of Education, Winneba (research.canil.ca/ATRLecture/Phonetics of ATR.pdf), section 2, p. 2: in languages like Akan, expansion or contraction of the pharyngeal cavity is a better measure of the [ATR] contrast than tongue root position alone; the IPA chart names the diacritics 'Advanced Tongue Root' and 'Retracted Tongue Root'
diacritics.reason: PanPhon writes ATR as [+tense] and RTR as [-tense]. Here [tense] has no part in vowel height, and [atr] is a feature of its own, so the mark sets [atr] and keeps [tense] as the base has it.

diacritics.name: Retracted tongue root
diacritics.source: Casali (2007), 'Some observations on the phonetics of [ATR] contrasts', lecture, University of Education, Winneba (research.canil.ca/ATRLecture/Phonetics of ATR.pdf), section 2, p. 2: in languages like Akan, expansion or contraction of the pharyngeal cavity is a better measure of the [ATR] contrast than tongue root position alone; the IPA chart names the diacritics 'Advanced Tongue Root' and 'Retracted Tongue Root'
diacritics.reason: PanPhon writes ATR as [+tense] and RTR as [-tense]. Here [tense] has no part in vowel height, and [atr] is a feature of its own, so the mark sets [atr] and keeps [tense] as the base has it.

diacritics.name: Palatalized
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Palatalized'; the feature is this table's
diacritics.reason: PanPhon writes the mark with the primary place features ['hi', 'back'], so it overwrote the base's place: in PanPhon kʲ and qʲ share a vector. The secondary articulation adds to the primary place and does not replace it, so the mark sets a feature of its own and the base keeps its place. The feature names are this table's.

diacritics.name: Labio-palatalized
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritics are named 'Labialized' and 'Palatalized'; the combined mark and the feature names are this table's
diacritics.reason: PanPhon writes the mark with the primary place features ['hi', 'back', 'round'], so it overwrote the base's place: in PanPhon kʲ and qʲ share a vector. The secondary articulation adds to the primary place and does not replace it, so the mark sets a feature of its own and the base keeps its place. The feature names are this table's.

diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Labialized'; the feature is this table's

The secondary articulation adds to the primary place and does not replace it, so the mark sets a feature of its own and the base keeps its place. The feature names are this table's.

diacritics.name: Velarized
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Velarized'; the feature is this table's
diacritics.reason: PanPhon writes the mark with the primary place features ['hi', 'back'], so it overwrote the base's place: in PanPhon kʲ and qʲ share a vector. The secondary articulation adds to the primary place and does not replace it, so the mark sets a feature of its own and the base keeps its place. The feature names are this table's.

diacritics.name: Velarized or pharyngealized
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Velarized or pharyngealized'
diacritics.reason: The chart leaves the place open, so the mark sets both [velarized] and [pharyngealized] to 0: one of the two, not known which. The base keeps its place.

diacritics.name: Pharyngealized
diacritics.source: McCarthy (1994), 'The phonetics and phonology of Semitic pharyngeals', in Keating (ed.), Phonological Structure and Phonetic Form: Papers in Laboratory Phonology III, Cambridge University Press, pp. 218-219: the emphatics have 'a constriction in the upper pharynx' and 'The so-called pharyngealized consonants of Arabic should really be called uvularized.'; Hermes, Barlaz, Shosted, Liang and Sutton (2017), Interspeech 2017, pp. 201-205: 'a clear difference in place' between pharyngealized and pharyngeal consonants (p. 204); Al-Solami (2017), Canadian Acoustics 45(1), pp. 25-35: emphatics show 'tongue root and tongue dorsum retraction with inconsistent tongue root retraction'; the IPA chart names the diacritic 'Pharyngealized'
diacritics.reason: PanPhon writes the mark as [+low, +back], which overwrote the base's place. Pharyngealized (emphatic) sounds constrict the upper pharynx with the tongue dorsum, at a different place from the pharyngeals (Hermes et al. 2017), and retract the tongue root inconsistently (Al-Solami 2017). The mark sets its own feature, [+pharyngealized], plus [-atr] for the tongue-root part, and keeps the base's place.

diacritics.name: Rhoticity
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Rhoticity'
diacritics.reason: PanPhon's rule gives [+high, +round, -anterior], so [ɚ] came out high and rounded. The chart names the mark only. This table reads it as a colouring that keeps the vowel's height and rounding, and keeps PanPhon's [-anterior].

diacritics.name: Voiceless
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Voiceless'
diacritics.reason: PanPhon applies the mark only to voiced sonorants, so [d̥] could not be read. It devoices any base.

diacritics.name: Voiced
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Voiced'
diacritics.reason: PanPhon has no rule for the mark. It voices any base.

diacritics.name: Raised
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Raised'
diacritics.reason: PanPhon's rule changes no feature. This table reads the mark as one chart row closer.

diacritics.name: Lowered
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Lowered'
diacritics.reason: PanPhon's rule changes no feature. This table reads the mark as one chart row more open.

diacritics.name: Advanced
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Advanced'
diacritics.reason: PanPhon's rule changes no feature. On a vowel this table reads the mark as one chart column further front.

diacritics.name: Retracted

diacritics.reason: PanPhon has no rule for the mark. On a vowel this table reads it as one step up the rounding scale -, 0, +.

diacritics.name: Less rounded
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Less rounded'
diacritics.reason: PanPhon has no rule for the mark. On a vowel this table reads it as one step down the rounding scale -, 0, +.

diacritics.name: Mid-centralized
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Mid-centralized'
diacritics.reason: PanPhon has no rule for the mark. On a vowel this table reads it as the central column, one row nearer mid.

diacritics.name: No audible release
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'No audible release'
diacritics.reason: PanPhon has no rule for the mark. No feature of this table encodes release, so the mark is read and changes nothing.

diacritics.name: Half-long
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Half-long'
diacritics.reason: PanPhon has no rule for the mark. It sets [long] to 0, between short and long.

diacritics.name: Breathy-voiced release
diacritics.source: This table's reading: the IPA chart (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005') lists 'ʰ Aspirated' and '◌̤ Breathy voiced' but not ʱ
diacritics.reason: PanPhon has no rule for ʱ, which inventories such as PHOIBLE write for voiced aspirates (bʱ, ɡʱ). It reads as ◌̤ on a voiced base: voiced, with spread glottis, as bʰ and b̤ already are.

diacritics.name: Ring above
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'), PDF p. 1: the note under the diacritics reads 'Some diacritics may be placed above a symbol with a descender, e.g.' and prints ŋ̊, the 'Voiceless' ring set above
diacritics.reason: The chart prints the ring above a descender as the ring of 'Voiceless'. The mark takes the rule of ◌̥.

diacritics.name: Dental
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'), PDF p. 1: the diacritic is named 'Dental'; The Unicode Standard 18.0 code chart U0300, https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0300.pdf (footer 'The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0, Copyright © 1991-2026 Unicode, Inc.'), PDF p. 4: '032A COMBINING BRIDGE BELOW • IPA: dental'; PanPhon 0.22.2 lists eight segments of a letter plus ◌̪, and each differs from its bare letter in [distributed] alone, - to +
diacritics.reason: PanPhon has no rule for ◌̪. The rule is the one difference PanPhon records between its dental segments and their alveolar letters, on a coronal base.

diacritics.name: Retroflexion
diacritics.source: The Unicode Standard 18.0 code chart U0300, https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0300.pdf (footer 'The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0, Copyright © 1991-2026 Unicode, Inc.'), PDF p. 4: '0322 COMBINING RETROFLEX HOOK BELOW • IPA: retroflexion'; International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'), PDF p. 1: the retroflex column
diacritics.reason: The mark makes a coronal base retroflex. Every retroflex letter of this table (ʈ ɖ ɳ ɭ ɻ ɽ ʂ ʐ) is [+coronal, -anterior], and every alveolar letter is [+anterior].

diacritics.name: Equals sign below
diacritics.source: The Unicode Standard 18.0 code chart U0300, https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0300.pdf (footer 'The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0, Copyright © 1991-2026 Unicode, Inc.'), PDF p. 5: '0347 COMBINING EQUALS SIGN BELOW • IPA: alveolar'; International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'), PDF p. 1: the alveolar column
diacritics.reason: The mark makes a coronal base alveolar. Every alveolar letter of this table is [+coronal, +anterior].

diacritics.name: Dot below
diacritics.source: The Unicode Standard 18.0 code chart U0300, https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0300.pdf (footer 'The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0, Copyright © 1991-2026 Unicode, Inc.'), PDF p. 4: '0323 COMBINING DOT BELOW • IPA: closer variety of vowel'
diacritics.reason: On a vowel the mark moves one row toward close, as ◌̝ does. The one-row step is this table's.

diacritics.name: Circumflex accent below
diacritics.source: The Unicode Standard 18.0 code chart U0300, https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0300.pdf (footer 'The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0, Copyright © 1991-2026 Unicode, Inc.'), PDF p. 4: '032D COMBINING CIRCUMFLEX ACCENT BELOW • Americanist: fronted articulation'; the same chart gives ◌̟ the annotation 'IPA: advanced or fronted articulation'
diacritics.reason: The chart gives ◌̭ and ◌̟ the same meaning, fronted articulation, so ◌̭ takes the rule of ◌̟.

diacritics.name: Strong articulation
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, extIPA symbols for disordered speech (revised to 2015), https://www.internationalphoneticassociation.org/sites/default/files/extIPA_2016.pdf (footer '© ICPLA 2015'), PDF p. 1: the mark is named 'strong articulation'; The Unicode Standard 18.0 code chart U0300, https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0300.pdf (footer 'The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0, Copyright © 1991-2026 Unicode, Inc.'), PDF p. 5: '0348 COMBINING DOUBLE VERTICAL LINE BELOW • IPA: strong articulation'
diacritics.reason: Neither chart gives the mark a laryngeal or place meaning, so it reads and changes no feature, as ◌̚ does. Korean fortis obstruents are written with the mark, and they read as their plain letters.

diacritics.name: Weak articulation
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, extIPA symbols for disordered speech (revised to 2015), https://www.internationalphoneticassociation.org/sites/default/files/extIPA_2016.pdf (footer '© ICPLA 2015'), PDF p. 1: the mark is named 'weak articulation'; The Unicode Standard 18.0 code chart U0300, https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0300.pdf (footer 'The Unicode Standard, Version 18.0, Copyright © 1991-2026 Unicode, Inc.'), PDF p. 5: '0349 COMBINING LEFT ANGLE BELOW • IPA: weak articulation'
diacritics.reason: Neither chart gives the mark a laryngeal or place meaning, so it reads and changes no feature, as ◌̚ does.

diacritics.name: Nasalized
diacritics.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Nasalized' and the chart prints it on the vowel e, as ẽ
diacritics.reason: PanPhon applies the mark only to voiced bases. The chart prints it on a vowel and ties it to no voicing, so a voiceless vowel such as [ɐ̥̃] is nasalized. PanPhon's condition stays for consonants: a voiced consonant that is not nasal takes the mark, as [b̃ z̃ w̃], and a voiceless consonant or a nasal is refused, as [k̃ m̃].

diacritics.name: Syllabic
diacritics.source: The Unicode Standard 18.0 code chart U0250 (IPA Extensions), PDF p. 5, under 'Sinological extension': '027F ɿ ... apical dental vowel ... IPA spelling - 007A z 0329', the mark on a fricative; International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): the diacritic is named 'Syllabic'
diacritics.reason: PanPhon applies the mark to a continuant only if it has no delayed release, so [ɮ̩] could not be read. The Unicode chart spells a syllabic fricative with the mark, so it applies to any fricative. Syllabic vowels and stops stay refused.

segments.name: voiced labiodental flap
segments.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'): pulmonic consonants, Tap or Flap row, Labiodental column

segments.name: voiceless epiglottal fricative
segments.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'), Other Symbols: the letter is named 'Voiceless epiglottal fricative' or 'Voiced epiglottal fricative'; Hassan, Esling, Moisik and Crevier-Buchman (2011), 'Aryepiglottic trilled variants of /ʕ, ħ/ in Iraqi Arabic', Proceedings of ICPhS XVII, Hong Kong, pp. 831-834, p. 831: 'both pharyngeals and epiglottals occur at the aryepiglottic sphincter point of stricture', and sounds described as epiglottal 'are associated either with AE trilled varieties of the simple fricative or approximant or with the default raised-larynx posture of the laryngeal sphincter'; this table takes the trilled reading
segments.reason: PanPhon does not list the symbol. It is the pharyngeal fricative [ħ] made by the aryepiglottic folds, with trilling.

segments.name: voiced epiglottal fricative
segments.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'), Other Symbols: the letter is named 'Voiceless epiglottal fricative' or 'Voiced epiglottal fricative'; Hassan, Esling, Moisik and Crevier-Buchman (2011), 'Aryepiglottic trilled variants of /ʕ, ħ/ in Iraqi Arabic', Proceedings of ICPhS XVII, Hong Kong, pp. 831-834, p. 831: 'both pharyngeals and epiglottals occur at the aryepiglottic sphincter point of stricture', and sounds described as epiglottal 'are associated either with AE trilled varieties of the simple fricative or approximant or with the default raised-larynx posture of the laryngeal sphincter'; this table takes the trilled reading
segments.reason: PanPhon does not list the symbol. It is the voiced counterpart of [ʜ].

segments.name: epiglottal plosive
segments.source: International Phonetic Association, The IPA Chart, IPA_Kiel.pdf at internationalphoneticassociation.org (footer 'IPA Chart revised to 2015/2005'), Other Symbols: 'Epiglottal plosive'
segments.reason: PanPhon does not list the symbol. The chart lists it under Other Symbols as 'Epiglottal plosive'. It is built as a voiceless stop at the pharyngeal place.

segments.name: voiced alveolo-palatal nasal
segments.source: Unicode Standard 18.0 code chart U0180 (Latin Extended-B), PDF p. 8, heading 'Additions for Sinology': '0235 LATIN SMALL LETTER N WITH CURL'; the chart U0250 (IPA Extensions), PDF p. 3, annotates ɕ 'LATIN SMALL LETTER C WITH CURL' as 'voiceless alveolo-palatal laminal fricative', and the curl is that of ɕ and ʑ; Wikipedia, 'Voiced palatal nasal': 'There is a non-IPA letter, ⟨ȵ⟩ (i.e. ⟨n⟩, plus the curl found in the symbols for alveolo-palatal sibilant fricatives ⟨ɕ, ʑ⟩), which is used especially in Sinological circles' (the sound is the voiced alveolo-palatal nasal); PHOIBLE 2.0 lists ȵ with [+coronal, +dorsal, +high, -low, +front, -back, +distributed]. segments.name: voiced retroflex implosive
segments.source: Unicode Standard 18.0 code chart U1D80 (Latin Extensions Supplement), PDF p. 3: '1D91 ᶑ LATIN SMALL LETTER D WITH HOOK AND TAIL', in the block 'Latin letters with retroflex hook'; Wikipedia, 'Voiced retroflex implosive': 'The implicit symbol in the International Phonetic Alphabet is ⟨ᶑ⟩ (a D with a tail for retroflex and a hook-top for implosive)'; PHOIBLE 2.0 lists ᶑ with [+coronal, -anterior, -distributed, +periodicGlottalSource, +loweredLarynxImplosive]. segments.name: apical dental vowel
segments.source: Unicode Standard 18.0 code chart U0250 (IPA Extensions), PDF p. 5, under 'Sinological extension': '027F ɿ LATIN SMALL LETTER REVERSED R WITH FISHHOOK ... apical dental vowel ... IPA spelling - 007A z 0329' (z with U+0329, the syllabic mark)
segments.reason: PanPhon does not list the letter. The chart gives its IPA spelling as a syllabic [z], so it has the vector of [z̩]: [z] with [syl] +.

segments.name: labialized apical dental vowel
segments.source: Unicode Standard 18.0 code chart U0250 (IPA Extensions), PDF p. 6, under 'Sinological extensions': '02AE ʮ LATIN SMALL LETTER TURNED H WITH FISHHOOK ... labialized apical dental vowel'; the apical dental vowel is ɿ, which the chart (page 5) spells 'z' with U+0329
segments.reason: PanPhon does not list the letter. Labialized on a syllabic segment is lip rounding, which the table codes as [round] + and [lab] + (as in [y]). So it is [ɿ], that is [z̩], with those two values.
